requirements.evidence: .env.example sets APP_NAME=PegaFila/APP_LOCALE=pt_BR; phpunit.xml:21-24 pins APP_NAME, APP_LOCALE, APP_FALLBACK_LOCALE; config/mail.php:112 'theme' => 'pegafila' with pegafila.css using #0f7490 on .button-primary (inlined on the action button); lang/pt_BR.json adds "Reset your password" and "Verify your email address"; routes/web.php:16-27 define password.request/email (throttle:6,1)/reset/update under guest, verification.verify with auth+signed+throttle; PasswordResetLinkController::store always returns back()->with('status', __('passwords.sent')); NewPasswordController::store validates min(8)->letters()->mixedCase()->numbers() + confirmed, rotates remember_token, fires PasswordReset, redirects to '/'; VerifyEmailController uses EmailVerificationRequest (403 on mismatch) and redirects to '/'.

conventions.evidence: Tests ship with the change; CHANGELOG.md and docs/business-rules.md updated; Bulma markup with labels. Deviations: NewPasswordController::store validates three fields inline ('token','email','password') where conventions ask for a Form Request beyond one or two fields; the two auth views duplicate a full <html>/<head> skeleton rather than reusing a component (layouts were out of scope, so minor).

security.evidence: Reset-link request never reveals account existence (PasswordResetLinkController.php:29-31, tested); throttle:6,1 on password.email; strong password rule; remember_token rotated; verification uses EmailVerificationRequest + signed middleware; all view output escaped with {{ }} (e.g. value="{{ $token }}"); forceFill on a framework-controlled closure, no mass-assignment from request.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/AccountMailTest.php covers config pins, theme + brand color in rendered HTML, pt-BR subjects/greeting/button/body/subcopy and absence of English sub-copy; PasswordResetTest.php covers form render, existing vs unknown email (same response, no mail), validation, throttling (429), single e-mail input, successful reset (hash, remember_token, event), invalid token, password-strength dataset, guest-only; EmailVerificationTest.php covers notification URL, valid link, wrong hash, other user id, unsigned link (403).

simplicity.evidence: Reuses Laravel's Password broker, EmailVerificationRequest and built-in notifications; no custom notifications. Some duplication: forgot-password.blade.php and reset-password.blade.php repeat the same head/@vite/CDN fallback block; pegafila.css is a full 299-line copy of default.css (acceptable for a theme).

readability.evidence: Small focused controllers with PHPDoc (e.g. 'The response is identical whether or not the address is registered'); clear route grouping; descriptive test names; no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task. Small extras: app/Models/User.php now implements MustVerifyEmail (not required for the notification/route and changes behavior for future registration), and config/mail.php adds 'paths' alongside the theme.

issues.explanation: Three-field validation is inline; conventions call for a Form Request once rules grow beyond one or two fields.
Both views duplicate the full HTML head including the @vite/CDN fallback instead of sharing markup.
Implementing MustVerifyEmail is not required by the task and will change behavior once registration fires the Registered event.
The reset endpoint returns the broker status (e.g. passwords.user) as an email error, which can distinguish unknown addresses; standard Laravel behavior and not required by the task.

review.summary: The change delivers the pt-BR account e-mails with a pegafila mail theme, the guest password-reset flow and the signed verification route, all built on Laravel's own broker and notifications, with thorough feature tests and updated docs/CHANGELOG. Remaining points are minor: inline three-field validation instead of a Form Request, duplicated view skeletons, and an extra MustVerifyEmail interface. Approve with nits.
